Measures
In this Attachment and Social Anxiety data set, the 3 scales refer to participants’ average scores on measures of social anxiety, attachment anxiety and self-esteem. The Social Interaction Anxiety scale is a 20-item survey that measures distress and fear experienced in social interactions (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.9). The shortened Attachment-Related Anxiety scale is a 9-item subscale of the Experiences in Close relationships Scale (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.94); it measures a person’s level of fear, insecurity, and hypervigilance regarding rejection, abandonment, and emotional distance in close relationships. The Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale is a 10-item survey that measures global self-esteem and overall feelings of self-worth or self-acceptance (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.85).


Data Analysis Strategy
The data for items SA_5, SA_9, and SA_11 on the social anxiety scale, and items SEst_2, SEst_5, SEst_6, SEst_8, and SEst_9 on the self-esteem scale scale were reverse coded.

Measures
In this BFI data set, the 5 factors refer to the 5 composites included in the Big Five Inventory. Openness, which indicates one’s open-mindedness, creativity, and likelihood to embrace new experiences (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.6). Conscientiousness, which refers to one’s tendency to be reliable, organized, and disciplined (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.72). Extraversion, which refers to one’s social interactions and emotional expression (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.76). Agreeableness, which refers to one’s tendency to cooperate or desire to compete (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.7). and Neuroticism which refers to one’s tendency toward depression, anxiety, or negative feelings (Cronbach’s alpha =0.81).


Data Analysis Strategy
The data for variables O2, C4, E1, E2, and A1 were reverse keyed.
